Grand Duke of Tuscany, 1790–1799. Grand Duke of the Habsburg-Lorraine dynasty.

Barnabas Chiaramonti, Benedictine born in Cesena in 1742, was elected in Venice in 1800. He signed the concordat with Napoleon (1801), attended his coronation (1804) and was his prisoner between 1809 and 1814; he died in 1823.
Lord of Milan, 1339–1349 (corregent). Lord of the Visconti dynasty.
Lord of Milan, 1339–1354 (corregent). Lord of the Visconti dynasty.
Dogo de Genoa, 1339–1344. Dogo.
King of Naples, 1414–1435. King of the Anjou-Durazzo dynasty.

Noble and military in the service of the Gonzaga of Mantua, father of Baldassare Castiglione and husband of Luigia Gonzaga. He died in 1499 after the wounds suffered in Fornovo. The card does not assign a year of birth without sufficient source.

Also called Aloisa Gonzaga, she was the wife of Cristoforo Castiglione and the mother of Baldassare. She participated in the decisions of his formation and corresponded with him. Her life dates are not completed from conjecture.
Wife of Baldassare Castiglione since 1516. Her death in 1520 preceded the ecclesiastical stage and the Spanish nunciature of her husband.

Writer, humanist and diplomat of the court of Urbino, author of El cortano, published in 1528. He served Gonzaga and the Dukes of Urbino and was nuncio of Clement VII to Charles V. He died in Toledo in 1529.

Diplomat of Italian origin, cardinal and chief minister during the regency of Anne of Austria and the youth of Louis XIV. Overcame the Fronda and intervened in the negotiations of Westphalia and peace of the Pyrenees.

She was born in Venice and trained in the French court. She composed poetry and political and moral treatises, and defended the intellectual capacity and dignity of women in The City of Ladies, written in 1405.

eventos.titulo: Marriage of Isabel of Castile and Fernando of Aragon
eventos.descripcion: The marriage union links the two main crowns of the Iberian peninsula without legally merging them into a single kingdom.
The capitulation of Granada to Isabel I and Fernando II put an end to the Nasrid emirate; Muhammad XII, Boabdil, handed over the city.

eventos.titulo: The Symbolic Beginning of the Lutheran Reformation
eventos.descripcion: The controversy over indulgences makes Martin Luther the center of a dispute that soon overflows academic debate and questions authority, doctrine and obedience.
Charles V demands Luther to retract. The refusal of the reformer and the political protection of Frederick the Wise transform a theological dispute into a constitutional problem of the Empire.
Imperial forces defeat the French army and capture King Francis I.
Imperial mutiny troops plunder Rome during the Italian Wars.
The agreement legally accepts the coexistence of Catholic and Lutheran territories within the Empire and recognizes that religious unity can no longer be restored by mere imperial imposition.
Charles V progressively splits his domains between the Spanish branch and the Austrian branch of the Habsburgs.

The fleet of the Holy League, led by Don Juan of Austria and composed mainly of forces of the Hispanic Monarchy, Venice and the Pontifical States, defeats the Ottoman navy of Ali Bajá after hours of galley combat against galley. The Ottoman center collapses, Uluç Ali manages to save part of his wing and thousands of fighters are killed, wounded or captives. Victory does not expel the Ottoman Empire from the Mediterranean, but destroys much of its combat fleet and becomes a huge political and symbolic triumph of the coalition.
Philip II's naval expedition against England fails after fighting, logistical problems and adverse temporary.

eventos.titulo: The White Company enters Italian politics
eventos.descripcion: Company of veterans of the Hundred Years War, including John Hawkwood's associate, make the mercenary condotta a decisive force of Italian politics.

eventos.titulo: Alberico da Barbiano y la Compañía de San Jorge
eventos.descripcion: Alberico da Barbiano symbolizes the consolidation of arms companies led by Italian captains, able to compete with the big foreign companies.

eventos.titulo: L'Aquila: fall of Braccio da Montone
eventos.descripcion: The L'Aquila war destroys the power of Braccio da Montone and accelerates the rise of a new generation of captains, including Francesco Sforza and Niccolò Piccinino.
The execution of Carmagnola shows the essential tension of the system: the states needed great captains, but feared that their private interests would end up imposing on those of the employer.

eventos.titulo: Francesco Sforza marries Bianca Maria Visconti
eventos.descripcion: Marriage introduces a condotiero to the succession of the Duchy of Milan and shows to what extent military force could be transformed into dynastic legitimacy.
Francesco Sforza culminates the most extraordinary career of a condotiero: from mercenary captain to founder of a ducal dynasty.
The peace between Milan and Venice inaugurates an Italian balance that reduces the political space for the great independent captains and favors armies more controlled by the states.

Cesare Borgia eliminates in Senigallia several captains who had rebelled against him. The episode, observed by Machiavelli, summarizes the conflict between the territorial prince and the autonomous condotiers.
The Venetian defeat of Agnadello shows the condotiers in wars already dominated by large international coalitions and armies of a much larger scale.
The death of Giovanni de' Medici after being wounded by artillery became a late symbol of the world of the great captains of fortune in the face of an increasingly transformed war by firearms.

eventos.titulo: Leonardo enters the service of the Sforza
eventos.descripcion: Leonardo settled in Milan and developed for years a career at the service of the court of Ludovico Sforza.
Leonardo portrays Cecilia Gallerani, lover of Ludovico Sforza. In 1491 Cecilia will give Ludovico a son, Cesare.
Bianca Giovanna Sforza belonged to the Milanese circle in which Leonardo’s first major court period took shape. A modern minority hypothesis has proposed her as the model for the Mona Lisa.

eventos.titulo: Leonardo in the service of Cesare Borgia
eventos.descripcion: Leonardo works as a military engineer for Cesare Borgia during his campaigns in central Italy.

eventos.titulo: The story of the Gioconda begins
eventos.descripcion: The traditional and now dominant identification relates the portrait to Lisa Gherardini, wife of Florentine merchant Francesco del Giocondo.
Leonardo returns to Milan under the protection of French governor Charles II d'Amboise.

eventos.titulo: Leonardo in the Rome of the Medici
eventos.descripcion: Leonardo settled in Rome under the protection of Giuliano de' Medici during the pontificate of Leo X.

eventos.titulo: Francis I calls Leonardo to France
eventos.descripcion: Leonardo moves to France accompanied by Francesco Melzi and enters the orbit of Francis I.
Leonardo dies in France. The Gioconda remained with him until his last years and ended up joining the French royal collection.
After the collapse of Hohenstaufen authority, several rival kings dispute an imperial crown whose capacity to impose obedience is greatly weakened.

eventos.titulo: Charles V is elected King of the Romans
eventos.descripcion: The succession of Maximilian I turns the imperial election into a European competition. Charles gathers the imperial crown with a dynastic heritage extending from the Netherlands to Spain and America.
In the absence of a male heir, Charles VI attempts to ensure the indivisibility of Habsburg domains and the succession of his future daughter Mary Theresa.

eventos.titulo: Francis I opens the Habsburg-Lorraine house
eventos.descripcion: The election of Francis Stephen returns the crown to the dynastic environment of Maria Teresa and creates the Habsburg-Lorraine line.
Joseph II succeeds his father as emperor and, after 1780, tries to quickly reform the Habsburg domains, repeatedly colliding with territorial and corporate privileges.
The revolution in France upsets the European political balance and makes the fate of Marie Antoinette, sister of Joseph II and Leopold II, an international dynastic problem.

eventos.titulo: Pope Francis II to Revolutionary Europe
eventos.descripcion: Francis II inherits the imperial crown in the midst of revolutionary war. Upon arrival 1800, the old Empire still exists, but faces a transformation that will culminate a few years later.
Philip Melanchthon presents to Charles V a systematic exhibition of Lutheran faith, supported by several princes and cities of the Empire.

eventos.titulo: Paul III approves the Society of Jesus
eventos.descripcion: The approval of the Society of Jesus gives institutional form to one of the most dynamic forces of Catholic renewal, active in education, missions and theological controversy.
The Council clarifies Catholic doctrine and approves disciplinary reforms in three major phases, under three pontificates, while the confessional division of Europe becomes permanent.
Charles V defeats the Esmalcalda League and captures its two great leaders, but the military victory fails to restore the religious unity of the Empire.
The last phase of the Council culminates in a programme of doctrinal definition and ecclesiastical reform that will shape the Catholicism of the Modern Age.

eventos.titulo: Nicholas III and the Rise of the Orsini
eventos.descripcion: The choice of Giovanni Gaetano Orsini as Nicholas III places one of the great Roman Baronial families at the center of the pontifical government and favors a wide network of relatives and clients.
The conflict between Boniface VIII and the Colonna turns a rivalry of Roman families into a political and ecclesiastical crisis of European scope.

eventos.titulo: Martin V and the Return of the Colonna
eventos.descripcion: The Council of Constance chooses Oddone Colonna as Martin V, closing the Western Schism and returning to Rome a recognized pontifical head.

eventos.titulo: Sixtus IV and the Della Rovere-Riario network
eventos.descripcion: Sixtus IV turns nephews Della Rovere and Riario into cardinals, rulers and pieces of a new family policy within the Pontifical States.
Rodrigo Borja ascends to the pontificate as Alexander VI and the career of his children makes the Borgia family an Italian political power.

eventos.titulo: July II and the Della Rovere restoration
eventos.descripcion: Giuliano della Rovere becomes July II and combines the territorial recovery of the papacy with a family network linked to Senigallia and Urbino.

eventos.titulo: The Medici arrive at the papacy
eventos.descripcion: Leo X takes the Medici house to the pontifical throne; a decade later his cousin Giulio de’ Medici will be Clement VII.

eventos.titulo: Paul III and the construction of a Farnese dynasty
eventos.descripcion: Paul III's pontificate combines Catholic reform with a dynastic policy that prepares the territorial ascent of his descendants in Parma and Piacenza.

eventos.titulo: Paul V and the rise of the Borghese
eventos.descripcion: The election of Camillo Borghese as Paul V makes Cardinal-nepote Scipione one of the great political, heritage and artistic beneficiaries of Baroque Rome.
Urban VIII elevates his nephews Francesco and Antonio to the cardinalate and Taddeo to the secular head of the family, also linked with the Colonna.

eventos.titulo: Innocent X, the Pamphilj and Donna Olympia
eventos.descripcion: The pontificate of Innocent X places Olympia Maidalchini in the center of the court and links the Pamphilj heritage with the Aldobrandini heritage.
Fabio Chigi becomes Alexander VII and calls his family to Rome; his nephew Flavio occupies the traditional place of the cardinal-nepote.

eventos.titulo: Innocent XI: a pope against the nepotist model
eventos.descripcion: Innocent XI avoids granting his nephew Livius the cardinalate and consciously limits the family privileges that had marked so many previous pontificates.
Innocent XII promulgates the constitution Romanum decet Pontificem, which formally restricts papal nepotism and closes a long stage of family rule of the Roman court.

The young Florentine chancellery sends Nicholas Machiavelli to negotiate with Caterina Sforza in Forlì. The mission places him before a ruler whose resistance and fall will reappear later in his reflections on fortresses, popular support and power.

eventos.titulo: The Prince arrives at Lorenzo de’ Medici
eventos.descripcion: The treatise drafted by Machiavelli after the fall of the Florentine Republic is finally dedicated to Lorenzo de’ Medici the Younger, Duke of Urbino and lord of Florence.

The accidental death of Henry II leaves the crown to Francis II. The youth of the new king elevates the influence of the Guisa and places Catherine de Medici in the face of a growing dynastic and confessional crisis.

eventos.titulo: Catherine of Medici directs the monarchy
eventos.descripcion: After the death of Francis II, Charles IX ascends to the throne while being a minor. Catherine tries to uphold the royal authority between the Catholic party of the Guisa and an increasingly organized Protestant nobility.
The massacre of Protestants in Wassy by men of the Duke of Guisa accelerates the uprising led by Louis de Condé and opens the first of the French Wars of Religion.

A few days after the wedding of Margarita de Valois and Enrique de Navarra, Coligny's assassination attempt leads to the killing of Huguenot leaders in Paris and a new wave of violence for the kingdom.
The death of Francis of Anjou makes Enrique de Navarra an alleged heir. Enrique de Guisa reorganizes the Catholic League, backed from Spain, to prevent a Protestant from inheriting the French crown.
The death of Frederick II leaves his kingdom of Sicily in the hands of a Hohenstaufen dynasty against the papacy. Conrad IV inherits the crown, while Manfredo maintains the family position in Italy.

eventos.titulo: Benevento: the Anjou take over the kingdom
eventos.descripcion: Charles of Anjou, backed by the papacy, defeats and kills Manfredo in Benevento. Hohenstaufen monarchy loses effective control of Sicily and Naples.
Conradino invades Italy to recover the inheritance of his family, but is defeated in Tagliacozzo and executed in Naples. Carlos de Anjou remains as owner of the former Hohenstaufen kingdom.
After years of war, the Sicilians support Frederick, son of Peter III and Constance of Hohenstaufen. The island develops its own political line in front of the Angevin Naples.

The peace of Caltabellotta recognizes Frederick on the island and the Anjou on the mainland. The old Sicilian monarchy is politically split between Trinacria and the kingdom that historiography will call Naples.

Alfonso V of Aragon defeats the Angevin resistance and enters Naples. For the first time since Vespers, the same monarch controls Aragon, Trinacria and the continental kingdom, although the crowns retain separate identities.

eventos.titulo: Alfonso's inheritance is once again separated
eventos.descripcion: At the death of Alfonso V, Aragón and Trinacria pass to their brother John II, while Naples remains for his son Fernando. Personal union does not become a stable fusion of crowns.

eventos.titulo: France and Aragon are distributed Naples
eventos.descripcion: Louis XII and Ferdinand the Catholic agree to divide the kingdom of Frederick I. Cooperation lasts little: disputes over the boundaries of partition make the former allies enemies.

eventos.titulo: Cerignola: the Grand Captain changes the war
eventos.descripcion: The forces of Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba defeat the French in Cerignola. The combined use of infantry, campaign fortification and firearms consolidates the Aragonese position in southern Italy.
A second great victory of the Grand Captain forces the French forces to withdraw. The balance born of the 1500 cast is definitely broken in favour of Fernando.

eventos.titulo: Ferdinand gathers Naples and Trinacria under his crown
eventos.descripcion: The French defeat leaves Ferdinand the Catholic as king of Naples in addition to Trinacria. The two parts of the former Sicilian monarchy once again share sovereign, although they will continue to be administered as distinct kingdoms.

eventos.titulo: The invasion of Cyprus forces Venice to seek allies
eventos.descripcion: The Ottoman offensive against Cyprus threatens one of the great Venetian possessions of the Levant. Venice needs to turn its particular war into a broader coalition.

eventos.titulo: Pius V gets the Holy League
eventos.descripcion: Pius V achieves an agreement between the Hispanic Monarchy, Venice and the Pontifical States. Philip II provides an essential part of the resources and his half-brother Don Juan of Austria receives the supreme command of the allied fleet.

In Messina, a heterogeneous army of Spaniards, Venetians, pontificals, genoese and other Italian contingents is concentrated. Coordinating different interests is almost as important as gathering the ships.

Pius V accompanies the coalition with public petitions, blesses the company and sends Don Juan a pontifical banner. Catholic memory will then associate victory with prayers and the Rosary; the tradition that the Pope knew triumph before receiving the news belongs to devotional tradition, not to a fact demonstrable by itself.

The League has Barbarigo in the left wing, Don Juan and Colonna in the center, Gianandrea Doria on the right and Alvaro de Bazán in the front of the reserve. In front of them, Ali Bajá directs the Ottoman center and Uluç Ali commands the wing that confronts Doria.

In the centre, the Royal Gallery of Don Juan and the Sultan of Ali Bajá are locked in a struggle of approaches, archabuces and successive reinforcements. Ali Bajá's fall and the taking of his ship disorganize the Ottoman center and make central combat the symbolic nucleus of victory.

eventos.titulo: The wings almost changed the result.
eventos.descripcion: Barbarigo is mortally wounded in the Christian left wing. At the opposite end, Uluç Ali takes advantage of the open space during Doria's maneuver and hits several League galleys. Alvaro de Bazán's reserve comes to close the gap, while Uluç Ali manages to withdraw with some of his boats.
Venice signs peace with the Ottoman Empire and renounces Cyprus. Lepanto has been an extraordinary naval victory, but not an Ottoman expulsion from the Mediterranean: the strategic balance continues.

eventos.titulo: Leopoldo and Sobieski agree on mutual relief
eventos.descripcion: With papal mediation, Leopold I and John III Sobieski agree on a defensive alliance. If Vienna or Krakow are attacked, the other sovereign must come to the aid of the ally.

eventos.titulo: From saving Vienna to moving on to the offensive
eventos.descripcion: After the victory a new Holy League was formed. Habsburg, Poland and Venice transformed an emergency defense into a prolonged war against the Ottoman Empire.

eventos.titulo: Frederick II recovers Jerusalem by treaty
eventos.descripcion: The Sixth Crusade temporarily returns Jerusalem to free control through negotiation, reinforcing the link of the Jerusalem crown with the Hohenstaufen.

eventos.titulo: The king's resignation does not force the island
eventos.descripcion: Jaime II agreed to abandon his Sicilian claim in Anagni, but the Sicilians refused to return to the Angevin domain. They chose their brother Federico and forced the Casa de Barcelona to divide over the future of the island.

Caltabellotta had foreseen Frederick’s lifetime government and a subsequent solution favorable to the Anjou. By associating Peter to the throne, the island house defended its own hereditary transmission. The peace of 1302 had not closed the dispute.

eventos.titulo: The death of the heir leaves the crown to a granddaughter
eventos.descripcion: Charles, Duke of Calabria died before Roberto. Juana inherited the crown and had to assert her authority in front of branches of her own family. The murder of Andrés de Anjou then triggered the invasions of Louis of Hungary.

eventos.titulo: Another peace redefines the two Sicilys
eventos.descripcion: The papal mediation gave a new framework to the recognition of Frederick as king of Trinacria, with obligations towards Joan. The names of Sicily and Trinacria expressed rights discussed in addition to a geographical separation.
Joan had chosen Louis of Anjou as heir, but Charles of Durazzo conquered the kingdom. His death and that of Joan left the next generation a war between Anjou and Durazzo, not a peaceful succession.

Mary and Martin came to Sicily with Aragonese support to impose themselves on the barons. The Queen’s hereditary legitimacy was not enough without military capacity. The island’s government was once again closely linked to the Crown of Aragon.
