personas.nombre: Frederick II of the Holy Roman Empire
personas.resumen: Emperor Hohenstaufen, king of Sicily and Jerusalem, an exceptional figure of the Mediterranean policy of the thirteenth century. His conflict with the papacy and his Sicilian court marked an entire epoch.
Latin Emperor of Constantinople since 1221, from the house of Courtenay. He lost much of his territory to Nicaea and Epirus.
He was the last Latin emperor to rule Constantinople. After the recovery of the city by the Byzantines, he sought in the West support to restore an empire that he only retained as a title.
Consort of the Brienne Dynasty. His career is linked to the Latin Empire.
Son of Baldwin II, last Latin emperor of Constantinople. After the Byzantine reconquest of 1261 he inherited only the title and married Beatrice, daughter of Charles of Anjou.
Consort of the Anjou dynasty. His trajectory is linked to Naples, Latin Empire.
Consort of the Courtenay dynasty, his career is linked to the Latin Empire.
Consort of the Angelo dynasty. His trajectory is linked to Germany, Byzantium.
He inherited the rights of the Hohenstaufen in Germany and Sicily in full struggle with the papacy. His death left Conrado, known as Conradino, as heir to a threatened cause.

Charles of Durazzo ruled Croatia and Dalmatia by delegation of Louis I before conquering Naples in 1381. His domains included Corfu and Butrinto; his authority over Achaia was nominal, in front of the local power of the Navarra Company. Coronado king of Hungary and Croatia on 31 December 1385, suffered an attack on Buddha in February 1386 and died shortly after. His title of Jerusalem did not imply control of the Holy Land.

The daughter of Charles of Valois and Catherine of Courtenay, inherited the title of Latin Empress of Constantinople, already without territory. Married to Philip of Tarento, she resided in the Angevin court of Naples.
The titular Consort of the Anjou-Hungary dynasty. His career is linked to Hungary, the Latin Empire, Tarento.
The titular Consort of the Anjou-Durazzo dynasty. His career is linked to Naples, Latin Empire, Tarento.
Last Hohenstaufen, grandson of Frederick II. At sixteen years old he tried to recover Sicily from Charles of Anjou; defeated in Tagliacozzo (1268), he was beheaded in Naples.

Daughter of King Janus of Cyprus, he married Louis of Savoy and brought to the Alpine court a direct connection with the Lusignans. His numerous offspring linked with France, Milan and the Cypriot succession itself.
Son of Andronicus II, associated with the throne as co-emperor. He led campaigns against the Turks and the Catalan Company without success, and died before his father in 1320.
Byzantine Emperor since 1328 after a civil war against his grandfather Andronic II. He lost almost all of Asia Minor to the Ottomans, but recovered Thessaly and Epirus.
Byzantine emperor during half a century of civil wars, first against John VI Cantacuceno and then before his son Andronic IV. His empire was reduced and taxed by the Ottomans.
Byzantine Emperor since 1391. Traveled through Western Europe seeking help against the Ottomans; Bayezid's defeat to Tamerlan in 1402 gave Constantinople a break.
Despot of Morea, 1428–1460. Despot of Morea of the Paleolog dynasty.
Consort of the Paleolog dynasty. His trajectory is linked to Byzantium, Russia.
Consort of the Hetúmida dynasty. His trajectory is linked to Armenia cilitia, Byzantium.
Daughter of Amadeus V of Savoy and wife of Andronicus III Paleologist. He was regent by his son John V during the civil war against John Cantacuceno (1341–1347).
Daughter of John VI Cantacuceno and wife of John V Paleologist, marriage that sealed peace after the Byzantine civil war of 1341–1347.
Daughter of Serbian lord Constantine Dragaš and wife of Manuel II Paleologist. She was the mother of the last two Byzantine emperors, John VIII and Constantine XI.
Consort of the Zaccaria dynasty. His trajectory is linked to Morea, Byzantium.
Count of Anjou who married in 1129 to Melisenda, heir of Jerusalem, and reigned with her since 1131. His son Godofredo Plantagenet was the father of Henry II of England.
Queen of Jerusalem since 1131, daughter of Baldwin II. She ruled with Fulco and then with her son Balduino III, until he took power in 1152. She was a great religious promoter.
King of Jerusalem since 1143, son of Fulchus and Melisenda. He took power over his mother in 1152 and conquered Ashkelon in 1153.
King of Jerusalem since 1163. He tried several times to conquer Fatimid Egypt; his death in 1174 coincided with the rise of Saladin.
Noble of the Courtenay-Edessa dynasty. His trajectory is linked to Jerusalem, Edessa.
Consort of the Comneno dynasty. His trajectory is linked to Byzantium, Jerusalem.
King of Jerusalem from the age of thirteen. Despite suffering leprosy, he personally led the kingdom and his army during the growing confrontation with Saladin.
Queen of Jerusalem since 1186, sister of Baldwin IV. She crowned her husband Guido of Lusignan, under whose reign Jerusalem was lost to Saladin in 1187.
Count of Jaffa and Ashkelon of the Aleramici dynasty. His trajectory is linked to Monferrato, Jerusalem.
Son of Sibilah of Jerusalem, crowned a child with his uncle Baldwin IV. He died in 1186 at barely nine years old, opening up the succession crisis that preceded the fall of Jerusalem.
Husband of Sibila and king of Jerusalem during Hattin’s defeat. After losing the capital, he continued the struggle and ended up establishing Lusignan power in Cyprus.
Queen of Jerusalem since 1190, daughter of Amalaric I. Her successive husbands, Conrad of Montferrato, Henry of Champagne and Amalarch of Lusignan, ruled the kingdom with her.
Lord of Toron of the Toron dynasty. His trajectory is linked to Jerusalem, Toron.
Marquis of Montferrato who defended Tyre in front of Saladin in 1187. Married to Elizabeth I of Jerusalem and elected king in 1192, he was killed days later.

Count of Champagne, he married Isabella I of Jerusalem during the Crusades. His career brought the French comital house to the government of the Latin kingdom. His daughter Alice later married Hugh I of Cyprus, extending this family network’s presence in the eastern Mediterranean.
Lord of Cyprus after his brother Guido and first king of the island in 1197. That same year he married Elizabeth I and was king of Jerusalem until his death in 1205.
Noble of the Ibelin dynasty. His trajectory is linked to Cyprus, Jerusalem.
Queen of Jerusalem since 1205, daughter of Elizabeth I and Conrad of Montferrato. She married John of Brienne and died shortly after giving birth to Elizabeth II.
French knight who became king of Jerusalem by his marriage to Mary of Montferrato in 1210. He led the fifth crusade in Damieta and was later co-regent of the Latin Empire of Constantinople.
Queen of Jerusalem since her birth in 1212, daughter of John of Brienne and Mary of Montferrato. Married in 1225 to Emperor Frederick II, she died when she gave birth to Conrad in 1228.
Daughter of Alfonso IX of León and Berenguela of Castile. He married John of Brienne, king of Jerusalem and later Latin emperor of Constantinople.

Daughter of Henry II of Champagne and Elizabeth of Jerusalem, he married Hugo I of Cyprus. He exercised regency functions and maintained rights and interests linked to both shores of the Mediterranean. His file connects the house of Champagne with Cyprus and Jerusalem, without reducing it to its later Navarre branch.
King of Cyprus since 1205, son of Amalaric of Lusignan. He participated in the fifth crusade and died in Tripoli in 1218.
Princess of the Lusignan dynasty. Her trajectory is linked to Cyprus, Jerusalem.

Son of Bohemundo IV and husband of Elizabeth of Cyprus. His son Hugo III inherited the Cypriot crown by the maternal line, retained the name Lusignan and brought to his descendants the genealogy of the princes of Antioch.

He succeeded Hugo II along the line of Elizabeth of Cyprus, his mother, and inaugurated the branch of Antioch-Lusignan. He tried to strengthen the royal authority in Acre, but he clashed with the autonomy of the Barons and with the Angevin claims over Jerusalem.
Consort of the Ibelin dynasty. His trajectory is linked to Cyprus, Jerusalem.
Son of Hugo III, king of Cyprus and titular of Jerusalem since 1284. He died in 1285 after a year of reign and succeeded him by his brother Henry II.
Last king of Jerusalem who ruled from Acre. After the fall of the city in 1291 he retained the title of Jerusalem while continuing as king of Cyprus.
Noble Frank of the Kingdom of Jerusalem. After Hattin organized the defense of Jerusalem and negotiated the surrender of the city to Saladin in 1187.
Noble Crusader and lord of Transjordania, famous for his incursions and for his aggressive policy against Saladin. He was executed after the battle of Hattin.
Count of Tripoli and one of the great barons of the kingdom. He acted as regent and was a central figure in the political struggles that preceded Hattin.
Consort of the Cantabrian dynasty. His trajectory is linked to Byzantium, Serbia.
Last Byzantine emperor. He died defending Constantinople during the siege of 1453, and his death was associated with the end of the Roman Empire of the East.

He regained Constantinople in 1261 and founded the last Byzantine imperial dynasty. He combined diplomacy and military intervention to contain Charles of Anjou; the marriages of his sons linked his house with the powers of the Black Sea.

The daughter of Michael VIII and sister of Andronico II, his marriage to John II brought together the courts of Constantinople and Trebizond. He supported the Georgian marriage of his son Alejo II, linking the Palaiologists to the networks of the Caucasus.

He agreed to the throne as a child and his minority opened the struggle between the Ibelin and Frederick II. Resistance to imperial intervention consolidated a Cypriot monarchy with a nobility capable of conditioning the government.

Daughter of Bohemundo V and wife of Henry I of Cyprus, he exercised the regency of the island by his son Hugo II. His presence in Acre shows how Antioch's family alliances also influenced the politics of Jerusalem.

His reign passed under regencies and ended without descent. The succession passed to Hugo III, grandson of Hugo I by female line and son of Henry of Antioch: the surname Lusignan continued in a new family branch.

The son of Hugo III and brother of Henry II, he held the post of condestable. He did not manage to reign, but his son Hugo IV inherited the crown after Henry's death. His marriage linked him to the Ibelin of Beirut.

personas.nombre: Eschiva of Ibelin, Lady of Beirut
personas.resumen: Heir of the lordship of Beirut, he lost his territorial base with the Mamluk conquest. Married to Guy of Lusignan, he was the mother of Hugo IV of Cyprus. His trajectory connects the loss of the continental states with the continuity of their families on the island.

He succeeded his uncle Henry II and established a new Lusignan branch. His marriage alliances brought the island closer to Bourbon and Aragon. He abdicated in favour of Peter I while retaining the titular dignity of Jerusalem.

personas.nombre: Alice of Ibelin, Queen of Cyprus
personas.resumen: Second wife of Hugo IV and mother of Peter I and James I. His offspring gave continuity to the Lusignan monarchy during the 14th century. It belongs to a generation other than the Elizabeth of Ibelin married to Hugo III.

He promoted expeditions against the Muslim powers of the Eastern Mediterranean and sought support in the European courts. The seizure and plundering of Alexandria in 1365 did not result in a lasting conquest. His assassination opened up a crisis within the Cypriot court.

personas.nombre: Eleanor of Aragon, Queen of Cyprus
personas.resumen: Wife of Peter I and mother of Peter II, he played a prominent political role after the murder of her husband. He intervened in the court struggles and in his relations with Genoa. He ended up returning to the dominions of the Crown of Aragon.

personas.nombre: John of Lusignan, Regent of Cyprus
personas.resumen: Brother of Peter I, he ruled during the minority of Peter II. The accusations and revenges that followed the assassination of the king confronted the members of the court. His title of prince of Antioch was nominal, as the principality had disappeared.

He inherited the crown as a minor after the murder of his father. The war with Genoa ended with the loss of Famagusta and burdensome obligations for the monarchy. He died without surviving offspring, so that his uncle James succeeded him.

The daughter of Bernabò Visconti, she married Peter II to strengthen relations between Milan and Cyprus. Her only daughter died a little. After widowing she returned to Italy; she should not be confused with Valentina Visconti, Duchess of Orleans.

He was elected king while he remained captive in Genoa. His release and return demanded concessions that maintained the commercial dependence of the island. After the death of Leon V he incorporated into his title the nominal crown of Armenia.

He shared with James I the Genoese captivity, during which Janus was born. As queen of Cyprus he linked the Lusignans with the house of Welf. The family experience of captivity marked the next generation of the monarchy.

Born during the captivity of his parents in Genoa, he attempted to recover margin from the Genoese. The Mamluk invasion of 1426 ended with his capture and imposition of tribute. His sons connected the island with Savoy and continued the dynasty.

personas.nombre: Charlotte of Bourbon, Queen of Cyprus
personas.resumen: The daughter of John of Bourbon-La Marche and Catherine of Vendôme, she married Janus. She was the mother of John II and Anne of Cyprus. This union directly connects the Lusignans with the Bourbons and, by Anne, with the Savoy dynasty.

He ruled an island subject to Mamluk tribute and with Famagusta in genoese hands. His court welcomed Greek influences reinforced by his marriage to Helena Paleologian. His sons Carlota and James then disputed the succession.

The son of Manuel II, he ruled the despotate of Morea in a stage of Byzantine expansion in the Peloponnese. His daughter Helena became queen of Cyprus, linking the last Palaeologists with the Lusignans.

Daughter of Theodore II of Morea and wife of John II, she favored the Greek institutions of Cyprus. She was the mother of Carlota. Her presence in the court allows to follow the links between the Lusignan Mediterranean and the last Byzantine world.

He inherited the crown of John II and defended it in front of his half brother James. After losing his last bastion he went into exile and maintained his dynastic rights, which would end up linked to Savoy. His effective government is distinguished from his subsequent claim.

personas.nombre: Louis of Savoy, King of Cyprus
personas.resumen: The son of Louis of Savoy and Anna of Cyprus, he married his cousin Carlota. His royal dignity came from that marriage and was then reduced to a pretense in exile. It should not be confused with his father, Duke of Savoy.

The son of John II, who was born out of wedlock, obtained Mamluk help to dispute the crown to Carlota and recovered Famagusta from the Genoese. Her marriage to Catherine Cornaro reinforced the Venetian influence. She died before the birth of her heir.

Noble Venetian married to James II, exercised regency during the brief life of his son and continued as queen after his death. The pressure of Venice ended with his abdication in 1489. His retirement in Asolo maintained a remarkable cultural projection.

He was born after the death of James II and inherited the crown under the regency of Catherine Cornaro. His death during childhood left his mother as queen and facilitated the advancement of Venetian tutelage over the island.

personas.nombre: Amalric of Lusignan, Lord of Tyre
personas.resumen: Brother of Henry II, he removed him from the government of Cyprus and exercised the administration of the island. His marriage to Isabella of Armenia connected the Lusignans with the succession of sackcloth. He was murdered, which allowed Henry to return.
Born as Yolanda, daughter of William VII, she adopted Irene's name when she married Andronic II Paleologist. Monferrato was linked to the Byzantine imperial court.

Wife of Alejo IV, she was the mother of John IV and David. Her identity must be distinguished from the same-named empress married to Alejo III. Registering both unions as one would produce an impossible genealogy.
Byzantine Emperor since 1195 after overthrowing and blinding his brother Isaac II. He fled Constantinople at the arrival of the fourth crusade in 1203.
Founder of the empire of Nicaea after the fall of Constantinople into the hands of the fourth crusade (1204). Coronated emperor in 1208, he consolidated the main Byzantine state in exile.
Emperor of Nicea since 1221. He expanded the status of Nicen in Asia Minor and the Balkans and prepared for the recovery of Constantinople. The Orthodox Church venerates him as saint.
Emperor of Nicaea between 1254 and 1258, son of John III Vatatzés. Erudite and author of theological works, he died young leaving a younger son, John IV.
Emperor boy of Nicaea since 1258. Michael VIII Paleologist, his co-regent, removed him after regaining Constantinople in 1261 and ordered blinding him.
The penultimate Byzantine emperor (1425–1448) sought Western help against the Ottomans and accepted the union of the Churches at the Council of Florence (1439).

eventos.descripcion: Mehmed II conquers Constantinople; Constantine XI dies during defense and the Byzantine Empire comes to an end.
After the collapse of Hohenstaufen authority, several rival kings dispute an imperial crown whose capacity to impose obedience is greatly weakened.
The death of Frederick II leaves his kingdom of Sicily in the hands of a Hohenstaufen dynasty against the papacy. Conrad IV inherits the crown, while Manfredo maintains the family position in Italy.
Conradino invades Italy to recover the inheritance of his family, but is defeated in Tagliacozzo and executed in Naples. Carlos de Anjou remains as owner of the former Hohenstaufen kingdom.
The young Balduino IV wins an unexpected victory over Saladin near Montgisard.
Saladin destroys the main army of the Kingdom of Jerusalem in Hattin, leaving the capital virtually helpless.
Balian de Ibelin negotiates the surrender of Jerusalem to Saladin after organizing the defense of the city.

eventos.titulo: Frederick II recovers Jerusalem by treaty
eventos.descripcion: The Sixth Crusade temporarily returns Jerusalem to free control through negotiation, reinforcing the link of the Jerusalem crown with the Hohenstaufen.
The fall of Acre eliminates the last great territorial center of the Kingdom of Jerusalem in the Holy Land; the crown has since survived as a dynastic title linked to Cyprus.
Joan had chosen Louis of Anjou as heir, but Charles of Durazzo conquered the kingdom. His death and that of Joan left the next generation a war between Anjou and Durazzo, not a peaceful succession.

people.resumen: Noble of the Árpád dynasty. His trajectory is linked to Byzantium.

He reduced the military resources of the Byzantine Empire in a context of serious fiscal difficulties. The arrival of the Catalan Company and the war with his grandson Andronic III aggravated the crisis.

Daughter of Theodore II of Morea and wife of John II, she favored the Greek institutions of Cyprus. She was the mother of Carlota. Her presence in the court allows to follow the links between the Lusignan Mediterranean and the last Byzantine world.

He inherited the crown of John II and defended it in front of his half brother James. After losing his last bastion he went into exile and maintained his dynastic rights, which would end up linked to Savoy. His effective government is distinguished from his subsequent claim.

people.nombre: Louis of Savoy, King of Cyprus
people.resumen: The son of Louis of Savoy and Anna of Cyprus, he married his cousin Carlota. His royal dignity came from that marriage and was then reduced to a pretense in exile. It should not be confused with his father, Duke of Savoy.

The son of John II, who was born out of wedlock, obtained Mamluk help to dispute the crown to Carlota and recovered Famagusta from the Genoese. Her marriage to Catherine Cornaro reinforced the Venetian influence. She died before the birth of her heir.

Noble Venetian married to James II, exercised regency during the brief life of his son and continued as queen after his death. The pressure of Venice ended with his abdication in 1489. His retirement in Asolo maintained a remarkable cultural projection.

He was born after the death of James II and inherited the crown under the regency of Catherine Cornaro. His death during childhood left his mother as queen and facilitated the advancement of Venetian tutelage over the island.

people.nombre: Amalric of Lusignan, Lord of Tyre
people.resumen: Brother of Henry II, he removed him from the government of Cyprus and exercised the administration of the island. His marriage to Isabella of Armenia connected the Lusignans with the succession of sackcloth. He was murdered, which allowed Henry to return.
Born as Yolanda, daughter of William VII, she adopted Irene's name when she married Andronic II Paleologist. Monferrato was linked to the Byzantine imperial court.

Wife of Alejo IV, she was the mother of John IV and David. Her identity must be distinguished from the same-named empress married to Alejo III. Registering both unions as one would produce an impossible genealogy.
Byzantine Emperor since 1195 after overthrowing and blinding his brother Isaac II. He fled Constantinople at the arrival of the fourth crusade in 1203.
Founder of the empire of Nicaea after the fall of Constantinople into the hands of the fourth crusade (1204). Coronated emperor in 1208, he consolidated the main Byzantine state in exile.
Emperor of Nicea since 1221. He expanded the status of Nicen in Asia Minor and the Balkans and prepared for the recovery of Constantinople. The Orthodox Church venerates him as saint.
Emperor of Nicaea between 1254 and 1258, son of John III Vatatzés. Erudite and author of theological works, he died young leaving a younger son, John IV.
Emperor boy of Nicaea since 1258. Michael VIII Paleologist, his co-regent, removed him after regaining Constantinople in 1261 and ordered blinding him.
The penultimate Byzantine emperor (1425–1448) sought Western help against the Ottomans and accepted the union of the Churches at the Council of Florence (1439).

name: Naples
summary: The separation of 1282 left the mainland kingdom to the Angevins, although they continued to style themselves kings of Sicily. Charles II’s captivity, marriage alliances and claims to the island shaped the thirteenth century. Under Joan I, the Hungarian invasions and the struggle between Anjou and Durazzo turned the succession into a European conflict.
notes: A historiographical name for the mainland kingdom separated from the island in 1282. Its monarchs continued to use the title King of Sicily.

He inherited the continental crown while he was captive to the Aragonese. His liberation, marriage diplomacy and agreements with James II and Frederick articulated the Angioinian attempts to recover Sicily. His sons extended the family to Hungary, Tarento and Durazzo.
He made the court of Naples an important political and cultural center of the Mediterranean. His succession in favor of Joan I opened a stage of conflicts between Angevin branches.

He inherited Roberto's Naples and faced a crisis after the murder of her husband Andrés de Anjou. The invasions of Louis of Hungary, the power of her second husband Louis of Taranto and his election of Louis de Anjou as heir turned the Neapolitan succession into a European conflict.

His domains included Corfu and Butrinto; his authority over Achaia was nominal, in front of the local power of the Navarra Company. Coronado king of Hungary and Croatia on 31 December 1385, suffered an attack on Buddha in February 1386 and died shortly after. His title of Jerusalem did not imply control of the Holy Land.
The adoption by Juana I gave him a pretense about Naples which contested Charles of Durazzo. His Angevin rights should not be confused with a continued dominion of the Neapolitan kingdom.

He inherited the crown of Charles III during the minority age and disputed the kingdom to Louis II of Anjou. His mother Margaret's regency ensured the continuity of the house of Durazzo; later extended his intervention to the politics of Rome.

A widow of Charles III, he exercised the regency of Naples by his son Ladislao. The dispute with the branch of Anjou forced to sustain power from reduced bases and to negotiate supports; his intervention preserved the rights of the house of Durazzo.
He managed to occupy Naples during a part of his dispute with Ladislao. The struggle for the Italian kingdom absorbed much of the resources and politics of his home.

persona.resumen: Emperor of the Holy Roman Empire and sovereign of a composite monarchy that reached the Iberian peninsula, Italy, the Netherlands and America. Philip I inherited the Franche-Comté, Artois, Namur and Luxembourg, as well as other Dutch territories. He later incorporated Frisia, Utrecht, Overijssel, Drente, Groningen and Guelders in a staggered form, between 1524 and 1543. He preserved the ducal dignity of Burgundy, but did not rule the Duchy incorporated into France. From 1535 he kept Milan under imperial control; the investiture and subsequent possession of Philip II must be distinguished from that government.

gobiernos.nota: His father gave him the kingdom in 1554, before the wedding with Mary Tudor.

persona.resumen: King of the Hispanic Monarchy at the time of its highest European and Atlantic projection. During his reign there were Lepanto, the dynastic union with Portugal and the great rebellion of the Netherlands.

eventos.titulo: Marriage of Isabel of Castile and Fernando of Aragon
eventos.descripcion: The marriage union links the two main crowns of the Iberian peninsula without legally merging them into a single kingdom.
The capitulation of Granada to Isabel I and Fernando II put an end to the Nasrid emirate; Muhammad XII, Boabdil, handed over the city.
Charles V demands Luther to retract. The refusal of the reformer and the political protection of Frederick the Wise transform a theological dispute into a constitutional problem of the Empire.
Imperial forces defeat the French army and capture King Francis I.
Imperial mutiny troops plunder Rome during the Italian Wars.
The agreement legally accepts the coexistence of Catholic and Lutheran territories within the Empire and recognizes that religious unity can no longer be restored by mere imperial imposition.
Charles V progressively splits his domains between the Spanish branch and the Austrian branch of the Habsburgs.

The fleet of the Holy League, led by Don Juan of Austria and composed mainly of forces of the Hispanic Monarchy, Venice and the Pontifical States, defeats the Ottoman navy of Ali Bajá after hours of galley combat against galley. The Ottoman center collapses, Uluç Ali manages to save part of his wing and thousands of fighters are killed, wounded or captives. Victory does not expel the Ottoman Empire from the Mediterranean, but destroys much of its combat fleet and becomes a huge political and symbolic triumph of the coalition.
Philip II's naval expedition against England fails after fighting, logistical problems and adverse temporary.

eventos.titulo: Alberico da Barbiano y la Compañía de San Jorge
eventos.descripcion: Alberico da Barbiano symbolizes the consolidation of arms companies led by Italian captains, able to compete with the big foreign companies.

eventos.titulo: L'Aquila: fall of Braccio da Montone
eventos.descripcion: The L'Aquila war destroys the power of Braccio da Montone and accelerates the rise of a new generation of captains, including Francesco Sforza and Niccolò Piccinino.

eventos.titulo: Charles V is elected King of the Romans
eventos.descripcion: The succession of Maximilian I turns the imperial election into a European competition. Charles gathers the imperial crown with a dynastic heritage extending from the Netherlands to Spain and America.
In the absence of a male heir, Charles VI attempts to ensure the indivisibility of Habsburg domains and the succession of his future daughter Mary Theresa.
Philip Melanchthon presents to Charles V a systematic exhibition of Lutheran faith, supported by several princes and cities of the Empire.
Charles V defeats the Esmalcalda League and captures its two great leaders, but the military victory fails to restore the religious unity of the Empire.
Rodrigo Borja ascends to the pontificate as Alexander VI and the career of his children makes the Borgia family an Italian political power.
The death of Francis of Anjou makes Enrique de Navarra an alleged heir. Enrique de Guisa reorganizes the Catholic League, backed from Spain, to prevent a Protestant from inheriting the French crown.

eventos.titulo: Benevento: the Anjou take over the kingdom
eventos.descripcion: Charles of Anjou, backed by the papacy, defeats and kills Manfredo in Benevento. Hohenstaufen monarchy loses effective control of Sicily and Naples.
Conradino invades Italy to recover the inheritance of his family, but is defeated in Tagliacozzo and executed in Naples. Carlos de Anjou remains as owner of the former Hohenstaufen kingdom.
After years of war, the Sicilians support Frederick, son of Peter III and Constance of Hohenstaufen. The island develops its own political line in front of the Angevin Naples.

The peace of Caltabellotta recognizes Frederick on the island and the Anjou on the mainland. The old Sicilian monarchy is politically split between Trinacria and the kingdom that historiography will call Naples.

Alfonso V of Aragon defeats the Angevin resistance and enters Naples. For the first time since Vespers, the same monarch controls Aragon, Trinacria and the continental kingdom, although the crowns retain separate identities.

eventos.titulo: Alfonso's inheritance is once again separated
eventos.descripcion: At the death of Alfonso V, Aragón and Trinacria pass to their brother John II, while Naples remains for his son Fernando. Personal union does not become a stable fusion of crowns.

eventos.titulo: France and Aragon are distributed Naples
eventos.descripcion: Louis XII and Ferdinand the Catholic agree to divide the kingdom of Frederick I. Cooperation lasts little: disputes over the boundaries of partition make the former allies enemies.

eventos.titulo: Cerignola: the Grand Captain changes the war
eventos.descripcion: The forces of Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba defeat the French in Cerignola. The combined use of infantry, campaign fortification and firearms consolidates the Aragonese position in southern Italy.
A second great victory of the Grand Captain forces the French forces to withdraw. The balance born of the 1500 cast is definitely broken in favour of Fernando.

eventos.titulo: Ferdinand gathers Naples and Trinacria under his crown
eventos.descripcion: The French defeat leaves Ferdinand the Catholic as king of Naples in addition to Trinacria. The two parts of the former Sicilian monarchy once again share sovereign, although they will continue to be administered as distinct kingdoms.

eventos.titulo: Pius V gets the Holy League
eventos.descripcion: Pius V achieves an agreement between the Hispanic Monarchy, Venice and the Pontifical States. Philip II provides an essential part of the resources and his half-brother Don Juan of Austria receives the supreme command of the allied fleet.

In Messina, a heterogeneous army of Spaniards, Venetians, pontificals, genoese and other Italian contingents is concentrated. Coordinating different interests is almost as important as gathering the ships.

The League has Barbarigo in the left wing, Don Juan and Colonna in the center, Gianandrea Doria on the right and Alvaro de Bazán in the front of the reserve. In front of them, Ali Bajá directs the Ottoman center and Uluç Ali commands the wing that confronts Doria.

In the centre, the Royal Gallery of Don Juan and the Sultan of Ali Bajá are locked in a struggle of approaches, archabuces and successive reinforcements. Ali Bajá's fall and the taking of his ship disorganize the Ottoman center and make central combat the symbolic nucleus of victory.

eventos.titulo: The wings almost changed the result.
eventos.descripcion: Barbarigo is mortally wounded in the Christian left wing. At the opposite end, Uluç Ali takes advantage of the open space during Doria's maneuver and hits several League galleys. Alvaro de Bazán's reserve comes to close the gap, while Uluç Ali manages to withdraw with some of his boats.

eventos.titulo: The death of the heir leaves the crown to a granddaughter
eventos.descripcion: Charles, Duke of Calabria died before Roberto. Juana inherited the crown and had to assert her authority in front of branches of her own family. The murder of Andrés de Anjou then triggered the invasions of Louis of Hungary.

eventos.titulo: Another peace redefines the two Sicilys
eventos.descripcion: The papal mediation gave a new framework to the recognition of Frederick as king of Trinacria, with obligations towards Joan. The names of Sicily and Trinacria expressed rights discussed in addition to a geographical separation.
Joan had chosen Louis of Anjou as heir, but Charles of Durazzo conquered the kingdom. His death and that of Joan left the next generation a war between Anjou and Durazzo, not a peaceful succession.

eventos.descripcion: Marriage links the Burgundian heritage with the Habsburgs and changes the political balance of Western Europe.
The agreement returns Artois and Franche-Comté to the inheritance of Mary of Burgundy, while the Duchy of Burgundy remains in French hands.
Charles V demands Luther to retract. The refusal of the reformer and the political protection of Frederick the Wise transform a theological dispute into a constitutional problem of the Empire.
Imperial forces defeat the French army and capture King Francis I.
Imperial mutiny troops plunder Rome during the Italian Wars.
The agreement legally accepts the coexistence of Catholic and Lutheran territories within the Empire and recognizes that religious unity can no longer be restored by mere imperial imposition.
Charles V progressively splits his domains between the Spanish branch and the Austrian branch of the Habsburgs.
After the collapse of Hohenstaufen authority, several rival kings dispute an imperial crown whose capacity to impose obedience is greatly weakened.

eventos.titulo: Rodolfo of Habsburg is elected King of the Romans
eventos.descripcion: The election of Rodolfo I closes the Great Interregno and places the Habsburgs at the centre of imperial politics for the first time.

eventos.titulo: Marchfeld and the Austrian Habsburg base
eventos.descripcion: The defeat and death of Otakar II makes it possible to consolidate the Habsburgic appropriation of Austria and Styria, the territorial base of a dynasty that will take generations to monopolize the imperial crown.

The coronation of Frederick III inaugurates an extraordinary dynastic continuity: except for a brief interruption in the eighteenth century, imperial dignity will remain linked to the Habsburgs and then to the Habsburgs-Lorraine.
The Worms Diet promotes common mechanisms of justice, public peace, and political organization that seek to make governable an Empire made up of hundreds of territorial powers.

eventos.titulo: Charles V is elected King of the Romans
eventos.descripcion: The succession of Maximilian I turns the imperial election into a European competition. Charles gathers the imperial crown with a dynastic heritage extending from the Netherlands to Spain and America.
In the absence of a male heir, Charles VI attempts to ensure the indivisibility of Habsburg domains and the succession of his future daughter Mary Theresa.

In the midst of the Austrian War of Succession, elector Wittelsbach Charles Albert obtains the imperial crown and demonstrates that dignity remains elective, even after centuries of Habsburg predominance.

eventos.titulo: Francis I opens the Habsburg-Lorraine house
eventos.descripcion: The election of Francis Stephen returns the crown to the dynastic environment of Maria Teresa and creates the Habsburg-Lorraine line.
Joseph II succeeds his father as emperor and, after 1780, tries to quickly reform the Habsburg domains, repeatedly colliding with territorial and corporate privileges.
The revolution in France upsets the European political balance and makes the fate of Marie Antoinette, sister of Joseph II and Leopold II, an international dynastic problem.

eventos.titulo: Pope Francis II to Revolutionary Europe
eventos.descripcion: Francis II inherits the imperial crown in the midst of revolutionary war. Upon arrival 1800, the old Empire still exists, but faces a transformation that will culminate a few years later.
Philip Melanchthon presents to Charles V a systematic exhibition of Lutheran faith, supported by several princes and cities of the Empire.
Charles V defeats the Esmalcalda League and captures its two great leaders, but the military victory fails to restore the religious unity of the Empire.

The relief army led by John III Sobieski, with Polish, Habsburgic and Holy Roman Empire forces, breaks the Ottoman siege of Vienna on September 12, 1683. Victory opens a new phase of the war in Hungary and reinforces the rise of the Habsburg monarchy in central Europe.
The death of Frederick II leaves his kingdom of Sicily in the hands of a Hohenstaufen dynasty against the papacy. Conrad IV inherits the crown, while Manfredo maintains the family position in Italy.

eventos.titulo: Hungarian rebellion opens a door to the Sultan
eventos.descripcion: Imre Thököly leads a Hungarian opposition to the Habsburgs and seeks Ottoman support. The internal conflict of the monarchy of Leopold I is mixed with imperial rivalry in central Europe.

eventos.titulo: Leopoldo and Sobieski agree on mutual relief
eventos.descripcion: With papal mediation, Leopold I and John III Sobieski agree on a defensive alliance. If Vienna or Krakow are attacked, the other sovereign must come to the aid of the ally.

The great Visir Kara Mustafa leads the Ottoman army to Vienna. Leopold leaves the capital and Ernst Rüdiger von Starhemberg organizes the defense while the fortifications suffer weeks of siege and minework.

eventos.titulo: Poles, Imperials and German Princes Meet
eventos.descripcion: Charles V of Lorraine coordinates the imperial forces and joins contingents from Bavaria, Saxony and other territories of the Empire. Sobieski arrives with the Polish army and assumes command of the relief operation.

eventos.titulo: From saving Vienna to moving on to the offensive
eventos.descripcion: After the victory a new Holy League was formed. Habsburg, Poland and Venice transformed an emergency defense into a prolonged war against the Ottoman Empire.
The conquest of Buddha shows that Vienna was not an isolated episode. The war begun in 1683 becomes a Habsburgic expansion by Hungary and permanently alters the balance of Central Europe.

eventos.titulo: Frederick II recovers Jerusalem by treaty
eventos.descripcion: The Sixth Crusade temporarily returns Jerusalem to free control through negotiation, reinforcing the link of the Jerusalem crown with the Hohenstaufen.

people.nombre: Frederick I of the Holy Roman Empire
people.resumen: Frederick I, called Barbarossa, was King of the Romans since 1152 and emperor since 1155. From the house of Hohenstaufen, he disputed power in Italy and participated in the Third Crusade. He left for land in 1189 and died drowned in the Saleph River on June 10, 1190, before arriving in the Holy Land. He was the father of Philip of Swabia.

Emperor of the Holy Roman Empire and sovereign of a composite monarchy that reached the Iberian peninsula, Italy, the Netherlands and America. Philip I inherited the Franche-Comté, Artois, Namur and Luxembourg, as well as other Dutch territories. He later incorporated Frisia, Utrecht, Overijssel, Drente, Groningen and Guelders in a staggered form, between 1524 and 1543. He preserved the ducal dignity of Burgundy, but did not rule the Duchy incorporated into France. From 1535 he kept Milan under imperial control; the investiture and subsequent possession of Philip II must be distinguished from that government.

name: Limburg
summary: The historic Duchy of Limburg must be distinguished from the modern provinces that share its name. Its succession dispute ended with John I of Brabant’s victory at Worringen in 1288. The title was thereafter linked to Brabant but remained a separate dignity. The expanded series focuses on the Brabantine line and its transmission to Anthony of Burgundy, his sons and Philip the Good; gaps in the underlying data should not be read as an absence of rulers.

uniones.titulo: The Burgundian inheritance, fief to fief
uniones.resumen: Marriage, succession, purchase, renunciation and conquest gathered different legal fiefdoms. The map must follow each effective government, not paint all domains since the ducal investiture.
uniones.instituciones: The Duchy of Burgundy, centred on Dijon, was a French fief; the County of Burgundy was an imperial fief. Nevers and Rethel passed to a junior branch. After 1477 France took the duchy; the claims of Mary and her heirs did not amount to possession.

Emperor of the Holy Roman Empire and sovereign of a composite monarchy that reached the Iberian peninsula, Italy, the Netherlands and America. Philip I inherited the Franche-Comté, Artois, Namur and Luxembourg, as well as other Dutch territories. He later incorporated Frisia, Utrecht, Overijssel, Drente, Groningen and Guelders in a staggered form, between 1524 and 1543. He preserved the ducal dignity of Burgundy, but did not rule the Duchy incorporated into France. From 1535 he kept Milan under imperial control; the investiture and subsequent possession of Philip II must be distinguished from that government.

personas.resumen: Worringen’s victory strengthened his dominance over Limburg. His career illustrates the importance of noble and urban alliances in the principalities of the Netherlands.

Heir to Charles the Bold since 1477 and Duchess titular of Burgundy. His marriage to Maximilian of Habsburg linked that house to the Burgundian Netherlands. The dispute with France over the duchy, Franche-Comté and Artois prevents presenting all the inheritance as territory that ruled without interruption.
Duke of Burgundy and builder of a powerful territorial state between France and the Empire. His court was one of the brightest in 15th century Europe.

Last Grand Duke Valois of Burgundy. He died before Nancy in 1477; the French Crown incorporated the duchy, while his daughter Mary inherited rights over the Netherlands and the Franche-Comté. The inheritance was disputed and did not remain as a united State.

The son of Mary of Burgundy and Maximilian of Habsburg, he inherited the Netherlands and, after Senlis (1493), the Franche-Comté and Artois. He preserved the dignity of Duke of Burgundy, although the duchy was under the French Crown. His marriage to Juana I took him to Castile and transmitted heritages other than Charles V.

Emperor of the Holy Roman Empire and sovereign of a composite monarchy that reached the Iberian peninsula, Italy, the Netherlands and America. Philip I inherited the Franche-Comté, Artois, Namur and Luxembourg, as well as other Dutch territories. He later incorporated Frisia, Utrecht, Overijssel, Drente, Groningen and Guelders in a staggered form, between 1524 and 1543. He preserved the ducal dignity of Burgundy, but did not rule the Duchy incorporated into France. From 1535 he kept Milan under imperial control; the investiture and subsequent possession of Philip II must be distinguished from that government.

King of the Hispanic Monarchy at the time of its highest European and Atlantic projection. During his reign there were Lepanto, the dynastic union with Portugal and the great rebellion of the Netherlands.
He ruled the Netherlands alongside Isabella Clara Eugenia. His regime sought to stabilize the Catholic territories and coincided with the Twelve Year Truce.
She exercised the sovereignty of the Netherlands alongside Alberto and then continued as governor. Her political role was much broader than that of a dynastic consort.

King of Spain during a period of great cultural brilliance and strong political crises. His reign, associated with the Count-Duke of Olivares, was marked by European wars and rebellions of Catalonia and Portugal.
Last Habsburg king of Spain. His lack of descent turned his succession into a European question and, after his death, triggered the Spanish War of Succession.

First Bourbon king of Spain. The War of Succession made him lose Milan, Naples and Sardinia; he recovered the latter briefly between 1717 and 1720. His peninsular and Italian domains followed different paths.
Duchess of Brabant, 1355–1406. Duchess of the Brabant dynasty.

personas.nombre: Charles VI of the Holy Roman Empire
personas.resumen: Emperor Habsburg and rival of Philip V in the War of Succession. His house ruled Milan, Naples and Sardinia on different dates; he exchanged Sardinia for Sicily in 1720. The Pragmatic Sanction sought to secure his inheritance to Mary Theresa.

Sovereign of the hereditary domains of the Habsburgs and one of the great figures of the eighteenth century. He defended his heritage in the Austrian War of Succession and promoted important administrative reforms.

personas.nombre: Joseph II of the Holy Roman Empire
personas.resumen: Emperor Habsburg associated with enlightened despotism. He tried to thoroughly modernize the administration, the Church and society of his territories through a very ambitious reform program.

personas.nombre: Leopold II of the Holy Roman Empire
personas.resumen: Emperor Habsburg of brief reign, succeeded after governing Tuscany. He moderated several reforms by Joseph II and faced the expansion of the French Revolution in Europe.

personas.nombre: Francis II of the Holy Roman Empire
personas.resumen: Last emperor of the Holy Roman Empire and first emperor of Austria since 1804. He fought revolutionary and Napoleonic France, dissolved the Empire in 1806 and married his daughter Mary Louise to Napoleon.

He succeeded John I in Brabant and Limburg. He married Margaret of England and was the father of John III. The marriage maintained the English connection of the duchy, while the two ducal dignitaries continued to be transmitted under one house.

He ruled Brabante and Limburg during the first half of the 14th century. His daughters Juana and Margarita took family rights on different paths. Juana’s succession and Margarita’s Flemish marriage prepared the disputes and agreements that brought the duchy closer to the Burgundys.

Son of Philip the Atrevido and Margaret of Flanders, he inherited Brabant and Limburg in 1406. The connection came from the brabanon ancestry of his mother. He died in Azincourt; his sons John IV and Philip of Saint-Pol later ruled before the inheritance of Philip the Good.

He inherited Brabant and married Jacqueline of Bavaria. The marriage drew him into the conflict over Holland, Zeeland and Hainaut, but did not permanently unite those inheritances. He was succeeded by his brother Philip of Saint-Pol.

He succeeded his brother John IV in Brabant and Limburg. He died without issue and the duchies passed to their cousin Philip the Good. This succession added a distinct Brabantine inheritance to the wider Burgundian possessions.

eventos.descripcion: Juan Sin Miedo is killed in Montereau. Felipe the Good inherits Burgundy and approaches the English side.
Juana is captured by Burgundian forces near Compiègne and ends up in English hands; she will be executed in Rouen in 1431.

eventos.titulo: Foundation of the Order of the Golden Toison
eventos.descripcion: Philip the Good founds the Order of the Golden Toison in the context of his marriage to Isabella of Portugal.
Philip the Good reconciles with Charles VII and breaks his alliance with England.
Charles the Bold succeeds Philip the Good and tries to consolidate a territorial block between France and the Empire.

eventos.titulo: Battle of Nancy and death of Charles the Bold
eventos.descripcion: Charles dies without a male heir. His daughter Maria receives an inheritance immediately disputed by Louis XI of France.
Marriage links the Burgundian heritage with the Habsburgs and changes the political balance of Western Europe.
The agreement returns Artois and Franche-Comté to the inheritance of Mary of Burgundy, while the Duchy of Burgundy remains in French hands.
Charles V demands Luther to retract. The refusal of the reformer and the political protection of Frederick the Wise transform a theological dispute into a constitutional problem of the Empire.
Imperial forces defeat the French army and capture King Francis I.
Imperial mutiny troops plunder Rome during the Italian Wars.
The agreement legally accepts the coexistence of Catholic and Lutheran territories within the Empire and recognizes that religious unity can no longer be restored by mere imperial imposition.
Charles V progressively splits his domains between the Spanish branch and the Austrian branch of the Habsburgs.
Philip II's naval expedition against England fails after fighting, logistical problems and adverse temporary.

eventos.titulo: Charles V is elected King of the Romans
eventos.descripcion: The succession of Maximilian I turns the imperial election into a European competition. Charles gathers the imperial crown with a dynastic heritage extending from the Netherlands to Spain and America.
In the absence of a male heir, Charles VI attempts to ensure the indivisibility of Habsburg domains and the succession of his future daughter Mary Theresa.

In the midst of the Austrian War of Succession, elector Wittelsbach Charles Albert obtains the imperial crown and demonstrates that dignity remains elective, even after centuries of Habsburg predominance.

eventos.titulo: Francis I opens the Habsburg-Lorraine house
eventos.descripcion: The election of Francis Stephen returns the crown to the dynastic environment of Maria Teresa and creates the Habsburg-Lorraine line.
Joseph II succeeds his father as emperor and, after 1780, tries to quickly reform the Habsburg domains, repeatedly colliding with territorial and corporate privileges.
The revolution in France upsets the European political balance and makes the fate of Marie Antoinette, sister of Joseph II and Leopold II, an international dynastic problem.

eventos.titulo: Pope Francis II to Revolutionary Europe
eventos.descripcion: Francis II inherits the imperial crown in the midst of revolutionary war. Upon arrival 1800, the old Empire still exists, but faces a transformation that will culminate a few years later.
Philip Melanchthon presents to Charles V a systematic exhibition of Lutheran faith, supported by several princes and cities of the Empire.
Charles V defeats the Esmalcalda League and captures its two great leaders, but the military victory fails to restore the religious unity of the Empire.
The death of Francis of Anjou makes Enrique de Navarra an alleged heir. Enrique de Guisa reorganizes the Catholic League, backed from Spain, to prevent a Protestant from inheriting the French crown.

eventos.titulo: Pius V gets the Holy League
eventos.descripcion: Pius V achieves an agreement between the Hispanic Monarchy, Venice and the Pontifical States. Philip II provides an essential part of the resources and his half-brother Don Juan of Austria receives the supreme command of the allied fleet.

eventos.titulo: Foundation of the Order of the Golden Toison
eventos.descripcion: Philip the Good founds the Order of the Golden Toison in the context of his marriage to Isabella of Portugal.
Philip the Good reconciles with Charles VII and breaks his alliance with England.
Charles the Bold succeeds Philip the Good and tries to consolidate a territorial block between France and the Empire.

eventos.titulo: Battle of Nancy and death of Charles the Bold
eventos.descripcion: Charles dies without a male heir. His daughter Maria receives an inheritance immediately disputed by Louis XI of France.
Marriage links the Burgundian heritage with the Habsburgs and changes the political balance of Western Europe.
The agreement returns Artois and Franche-Comté to the inheritance of Mary of Burgundy, while the Duchy of Burgundy remains in French hands.
Charles V demands Luther to retract. The refusal of the reformer and the political protection of Frederick the Wise transform a theological dispute into a constitutional problem of the Empire.
Imperial forces defeat the French army and capture King Francis I.
Imperial mutiny troops plunder Rome during the Italian Wars.
The agreement legally accepts the coexistence of Catholic and Lutheran territories within the Empire and recognizes that religious unity can no longer be restored by mere imperial imposition.
Charles V progressively splits his domains between the Spanish branch and the Austrian branch of the Habsburgs.
Philip II's naval expedition against England fails after fighting, logistical problems and adverse temporary.

eventos.titulo: Charles V is elected King of the Romans
eventos.descripcion: The succession of Maximilian I turns the imperial election into a European competition. Charles gathers the imperial crown with a dynastic heritage extending from the Netherlands to Spain and America.
In the absence of a male heir, Charles VI attempts to ensure the indivisibility of Habsburg domains and the succession of his future daughter Mary Theresa.

In the midst of the Austrian War of Succession, elector Wittelsbach Charles Albert obtains the imperial crown and demonstrates that dignity remains elective, even after centuries of Habsburg predominance.

eventos.titulo: Francis I opens the Habsburg-Lorraine house
eventos.descripcion: The election of Francis Stephen returns the crown to the dynastic environment of Maria Teresa and creates the Habsburg-Lorraine line.
Joseph II succeeds his father as emperor and, after 1780, tries to quickly reform the Habsburg domains, repeatedly colliding with territorial and corporate privileges.
The revolution in France upsets the European political balance and makes the fate of Marie Antoinette, sister of Joseph II and Leopold II, an international dynastic problem.

eventos.titulo: Pope Francis II to Revolutionary Europe
eventos.descripcion: Francis II inherits the imperial crown in the midst of revolutionary war. Upon arrival 1800, the old Empire still exists, but faces a transformation that will culminate a few years later.
Philip Melanchthon presents to Charles V a systematic exhibition of Lutheran faith, supported by several princes and cities of the Empire.
Charles V defeats the Esmalcalda League and captures its two great leaders, but the military victory fails to restore the religious unity of the Empire.
The death of Francis of Anjou makes Enrique de Navarra an alleged heir. Enrique de Guisa reorganizes the Catholic League, backed from Spain, to prevent a Protestant from inheriting the French crown.

eventos.titulo: Pius V gets the Holy League
eventos.descripcion: Pius V achieves an agreement between the Hispanic Monarchy, Venice and the Pontifical States. Philip II provides an essential part of the resources and his half-brother Don Juan of Austria receives the supreme command of the allied fleet.

people.resumen: His marriage to Elizabeth of Bohemia settled the Luxembourg on the throne of Prague. He participated in campaigns throughout Europe and died in Crécy, even though he had lost sight.

people.nombre: Henry VII of the Holy Roman Empire
people.resumen: First emperor of the house of Luxembourg. He tried to restore imperial authority in Italy, but his early death left incomplete a project that anticipated the rise of his dynasty.
Consort of the Brabant dynasty. His career is linked to Germany, Luxembourg.
Duke of Luxembourg, 1353–1383. Duke of the Luxembourg Dynasty.

Heir to Charles the Bold since 1477 and Duchess titular of Burgundy. His marriage to Maximilian of Habsburg linked that house to the Burgundian Netherlands. The dispute with France over the duchy, Franche-Comté and Artois prevents presenting all the inheritance as territory that ruled without interruption.
Duke of Burgundy and builder of a powerful territorial state between France and the Empire. His court was one of the brightest in 15th century Europe.

Last Grand Duke Valois of Burgundy. He died before Nancy in 1477; the French Crown incorporated the duchy, while his daughter Mary inherited rights over the Netherlands and the Franche-Comté. The inheritance was disputed and did not remain as a united State.

The son of Mary of Burgundy and Maximilian of Habsburg, he inherited the Netherlands and, after Senlis (1493), the Franche-Comté and Artois. He preserved the dignity of Duke of Burgundy, although the duchy was under the French Crown. His marriage to Juana I took him to Castile and transmitted heritages other than Charles V.

Emperor of the Holy Roman Empire and sovereign of a composite monarchy that reached the Iberian peninsula, Italy, the Netherlands and America. Philip I inherited the Franche-Comté, Artois, Namur and Luxembourg, as well as other Dutch territories. He later incorporated Frisia, Utrecht, Overijssel, Drente, Groningen and Guelders in a staggered form, between 1524 and 1543. He preserved the ducal dignity of Burgundy, but did not rule the Duchy incorporated into France. From 1535 he kept Milan under imperial control; the investiture and subsequent possession of Philip II must be distinguished from that government.

King of the Hispanic Monarchy at the time of its highest European and Atlantic projection. During his reign there were Lepanto, the dynastic union with Portugal and the great rebellion of the Netherlands.

King of Spain during a period of great cultural brilliance and strong political crises. His reign, associated with the Count-Duke of Olivares, was marked by European wars and rebellions of Catalonia and Portugal.
His Moravian dominions and interests in Brandenburg made him an important prince of the Luxembourgs. He was elected King of the Romans, but died before consolidating that dignity.
Duchess of Luxembourg, 1411–1443. Duchess of the Luxembourg dynasty.
Last Habsburg king of Spain. His lack of descent turned his succession into a European question and, after his death, triggered the Spanish War of Succession.

First Bourbon king of Spain. The War of Succession made him lose Milan, Naples and Sardinia; he recovered the latter briefly between 1717 and 1720. His peninsular and Italian domains followed different paths.
Duchess of Brabant, 1355–1406. Duchess of the Brabant dynasty.

people.nombre: Charles VI of the Holy Roman Empire
people.resumen: Emperor Habsburg and rival of Philip V in the War of Succession. His house ruled Milan, Naples and Sardinia on different dates; he exchanged Sardinia for Sicily in 1720. The Pragmatic Sanction sought to secure his inheritance to Mary Theresa.

Sovereign of the hereditary domains of the Habsburgs and one of the great figures of the eighteenth century. He defended his heritage in the Austrian War of Succession and promoted important administrative reforms.

people.nombre: Joseph II of the Holy Roman Empire
people.resumen: Emperor Habsburg associated with enlightened despotism. He tried to thoroughly modernize the administration, the Church and society of his territories through a very ambitious reform program.

people.nombre: Leopold II of the Holy Roman Empire
people.resumen: Emperor Habsburg of brief reign, succeeded after governing Tuscany. He moderated several reforms by Joseph II and faced the expansion of the French Revolution in Europe.

people.nombre: Francis II of the Holy Roman Empire
people.resumen: Last emperor of the Holy Roman Empire and first emperor of Austria since 1804. He fought revolutionary and Napoleonic France, dissolved the Empire in 1806 and married his daughter Mary Louise to Napoleon.
Count of Luxembourg, 1281–1288. Count of the Luxembourg dynasty.
Consort of the Avesnes dynasty. His career is linked to Luxembourg.

name: Austria Interior
summary: A dynastic complex comprising Styria, Carinthia and Carniola, distinct from the Duchy or Archduchy of Austria. The partition of 1564 assigned it to Charles II, whose line inherited Danubian Austria in 1619. The map approximates these lands through modern regions and does not presume uniform borders or administration.
notes: A dynastic grouping of Styria, Carinthia and Carniola; only components present in the underlying data are linked here.

eventos.descripcion: The election of Rodolfo I closes the Great Interregno and places the Habsburgs at the centre of imperial politics for the first time.

eventos.titulo: Marchfeld and the Austrian Habsburg base
eventos.descripcion: The defeat and death of Otakar II makes it possible to consolidate the Habsburgic appropriation of Austria and Styria, the territorial base of a dynasty that will take generations to monopolize the imperial crown.

The coronation of Frederick III inaugurates an extraordinary dynastic continuity: except for a brief interruption in the eighteenth century, imperial dignity will remain linked to the Habsburgs and then to the Habsburgs-Lorraine.
The Worms Diet promotes common mechanisms of justice, public peace, and political organization that seek to make governable an Empire made up of hundreds of territorial powers.

eventos.titulo: Hungarian rebellion opens a door to the Sultan
eventos.descripcion: Imre Thököly leads a Hungarian opposition to the Habsburgs and seeks Ottoman support. The internal conflict of the monarchy of Leopold I is mixed with imperial rivalry in central Europe.

eventos.titulo: Leopoldo and Sobieski agree on mutual relief
eventos.descripcion: With papal mediation, Leopold I and John III Sobieski agree on a defensive alliance. If Vienna or Krakow are attacked, the other sovereign must come to the aid of the ally.

The great Visir Kara Mustafa leads the Ottoman army to Vienna. Leopold leaves the capital and Ernst Rüdiger von Starhemberg organizes the defense while the fortifications suffer weeks of siege and minework.

eventos.titulo: Poles, Imperials and German Princes Meet
eventos.descripcion: Charles V of Lorraine coordinates the imperial forces and joins contingents from Bavaria, Saxony and other territories of the Empire. Sobieski arrives with the Polish army and assumes command of the relief operation.

eventos.titulo: From saving Vienna to moving on to the offensive
eventos.descripcion: After the victory a new Holy League was formed. Habsburg, Poland and Venice transformed an emergency defense into a prolonged war against the Ottoman Empire.
The conquest of Buddha shows that Vienna was not an isolated episode. The war begun in 1683 becomes a Habsburgic expansion by Hungary and permanently alters the balance of Central Europe.

people.nombre: Joseph I of the Holy Roman Empire
people.resumen: Emperor Habsburg during the Spanish War of Succession. He continued the policy of his father Leopold I and supported the candidacy of his brother Charles to the Spanish throne.

people.nombre: Charles VI of the Holy Roman Empire
people.resumen: Emperor Habsburg and rival of Philip V in the War of Succession. His house ruled Milan, Naples and Sardinia on different dates; he exchanged Sardinia for Sicily in 1720. The Pragmatic Sanction sought to secure his inheritance to Mary Theresa.

Sovereign of the hereditary domains of the Habsburgs and one of the great figures of the eighteenth century. He defended his heritage in the Austrian War of Succession and promoted important administrative reforms.

people.nombre: Joseph II of the Holy Roman Empire
people.resumen: Emperor Habsburg associated with enlightened despotism. He tried to thoroughly modernize the administration, the Church and society of his territories through a very ambitious reform program.

people.nombre: Leopold II of the Holy Roman Empire
people.resumen: Emperor Habsburg of brief reign, succeeded after governing Tuscany. He moderated several reforms by Joseph II and faced the expansion of the French Revolution in Europe.

people.nombre: Francis II of the Holy Roman Empire
people.resumen: Last emperor of the Holy Roman Empire and first emperor of Austria since 1804. He fought revolutionary and Napoleonic France, dissolved the Empire in 1806 and married his daughter Mary Louise to Napoleon.

name: County of Burgundy
summary: The County of Burgundy, or Franche-Comté, belonged to the Empire and must not be confused with the neighbouring duchy. After the succession war of 1477, the Treaty of Senlis restored the county to the House of Austria in 1493. Philip I transmitted it to Charles V in 1506, and Charles to Philip II in 1555–1556; their Burgundian ducal title did not signify control of the French duchy. The map uses three regions from the historical SVG as an approximation of the county.
notes: Franche-Comté, distinct from the duchy. The Treaty of Senlis restored it to the House of Austria in 1493; it passed to Philip I and Charles V as part of the Burgundian inheritance.

eventos.descripcion: John II of France handed over the Duchy of Burgundy to his son Philip, the origin of the Valois-Borgoña branch.

eventos.titulo: Marriage of Philip and Margaret of Flanders
eventos.descripcion: The marriage to Margaret of Flanders prepares the marriage of Burgundy with rich Flemish and burgundy territories.
Juan Sin Miedo is killed in Montereau. Felipe the Good inherits Burgundy and approaches the English side.
Juana is captured by Burgundian forces near Compiègne and ends up in English hands; she will be executed in Rouen in 1431.

eventos.titulo: Foundation of the Order of the Golden Toison
eventos.descripcion: Philip the Good founds the Order of the Golden Toison in the context of his marriage to Isabella of Portugal.
Philip the Good reconciles with Charles VII and breaks his alliance with England.
Charles the Bold succeeds Philip the Good and tries to consolidate a territorial block between France and the Empire.

eventos.titulo: Battle of Nancy and death of Charles the Bold
eventos.descripcion: Charles dies without a male heir. His daughter Maria receives an inheritance immediately disputed by Louis XI of France.
Marriage links the Burgundian heritage with the Habsburgs and changes the political balance of Western Europe.
The agreement returns Artois and Franche-Comté to the inheritance of Mary of Burgundy, while the Duchy of Burgundy remains in French hands.
Charles V demands Luther to retract. The refusal of the reformer and the political protection of Frederick the Wise transform a theological dispute into a constitutional problem of the Empire.
Imperial forces defeat the French army and capture King Francis I.
Imperial mutiny troops plunder Rome during the Italian Wars.
The agreement legally accepts the coexistence of Catholic and Lutheran territories within the Empire and recognizes that religious unity can no longer be restored by mere imperial imposition.
Charles V progressively splits his domains between the Spanish branch and the Austrian branch of the Habsburgs.
Philip II's naval expedition against England fails after fighting, logistical problems and adverse temporary.

eventos.titulo: Charles V is elected King of the Romans
eventos.descripcion: The succession of Maximilian I turns the imperial election into a European competition. Charles gathers the imperial crown with a dynastic heritage extending from the Netherlands to Spain and America.
Philip Melanchthon presents to Charles V a systematic exhibition of Lutheran faith, supported by several princes and cities of the Empire.
Charles V defeats the Esmalcalda League and captures its two great leaders, but the military victory fails to restore the religious unity of the Empire.
The death of Francis of Anjou makes Enrique de Navarra an alleged heir. Enrique de Guisa reorganizes the Catholic League, backed from Spain, to prevent a Protestant from inheriting the French crown.

eventos.titulo: Pius V gets the Holy League
eventos.descripcion: Pius V achieves an agreement between the Hispanic Monarchy, Venice and the Pontifical States. Philip II provides an essential part of the resources and his half-brother Don Juan of Austria receives the supreme command of the allied fleet.

persona.resumen: King of Aragon who consolidated the Mediterranean projection of the Crown after the Sicilian crisis. His diplomacy and alliances placed the house of Aragon at the heart of Western Mediterranean politics.
He participated as an infant in the conquest of Sardinia. His reign was conditioned by the interests of the different branches of the royal family and by the problems of Mediterranean expansion.
He returned Mallorca to his domains and fought against Pedro I of Castile. His reign reinforced the royal ceremonial and left an important autobiographical chronicle.
His court was distinguished by music, literature and ceremonial. He died without a surviving son and was succeeded by his brother Martin.
His death without a legitimate surviving heir opened the Aragonese interregno. The crisis was resolved with the Caspe Commitment and the election of Fernando de Antequera.
The Commitment of Caspe chose him to succeed Martin I, inaugurating the Trastámara branch of Aragon. Previously he had exercised the regency of Castile during the minority of John II.
King of Aragon and conqueror of Naples, where he established a court that became one of the great humanist foci of the 15th century.

King of Aragon and Navarre, central figure of the dynastic conflicts of the Iberian peninsula of the 15th century. He was the father of Fernando the Catholic and key piece in the expansion of the Trastámara.

King of Aragon and, together with Isabel I, protagonist of the dynastic union of Hispanic crowns. His politics combined peninsular consolidation, Mediterranean expansion and intense marriage diplomacy.

King of Spain whose government was dominated by the Duke of Lerma and by a initially more peaceful foreign policy. His reign saw the expulsion of the Moors and the beginning of the Thirty Years' War.

King of Spain during a period of great cultural brilliance and strong political crises. His reign, associated with the Count-Duke of Olivares, was marked by European wars and rebellions of Catalonia and Portugal.
He participated as an infant in the conquest of Sardinia. His reign was conditioned by the interests of the different branches of the royal family and by the problems of Mediterranean expansion.
His court was distinguished by music, literature and ceremonial. He died without a surviving son and was succeeded by his brother Martin.
Duke of Savoy who took advantage of the Spanish War of Succession to raise the rank of his house. He first became king of Sicily and then king of Sardinia.
Last Habsburg king of Spain. His lack of descent turned his succession into a European question and, after his death, triggered the Spanish War of Succession.

First Bourbon king of Spain. The War of Succession made him lose Milan, Naples and Sardinia; he recovered the latter briefly between 1717 and 1720. His peninsular and Italian domains followed different paths.

personas.nombre: Charles VI of the Holy Roman Empire
personas.resumen: Emperor Habsburg and rival of Philip V in the War of Succession. His house ruled Milan, Naples and Sardinia on different dates; he exchanged Sardinia for Sicily in 1720. The Pragmatic Sanction sought to secure his inheritance to Mary Theresa.
King of Sardinia and Duke of Savoy who continued the territorial expansion of his dynasty in northern Italy. He actively participated in the great European wars of the eighteenth century.
King of Sardinia and Duke of Savoy since 1773. The war with revolutionary France cost Savoy and Nice, ceded by the armistice of Cherasco in 1796.
King of Sardinia since 1796. French troops forced him to leave their continental states in 1798; he took refuge in Sardinia and abdicated in his brother Victor Manuel I in 1802.
King of Sardinia since 1802. He recovered Piedmont and Savoy in 1814 and obtained Genoa at the Congress of Vienna; abdicated in 1821 after the liberal Piedmontese revolution.
King of Sardinia between 1821 and 1831, brother of Victor Manuel I. He restored an absolutist government after the revolution of 1821 and was the last of the main line of Savoy.
King of Sardinia since 1831, of the Savoy-Carignano branch. He granted the Statute of 1848 and declared war on Austria; defeated in Novara (1849), abdicated in Victor Manuel II.

Husband of Mary of Sicily and son of Martin the Human. He reorganized the power of the island monarchy in front of the barons and died after a campaign in Sardinia. His death without a legitimate surviving heir aggravated the succession of the Crown of Aragon.

eventos.titulo: Marriage of Isabel of Castile and Fernando of Aragon
eventos.descripcion: The marriage union links the two main crowns of the Iberian peninsula without legally merging them into a single kingdom.
The capitulation of Granada to Isabel I and Fernando II put an end to the Nasrid emirate; Muhammad XII, Boabdil, handed over the city.
Charles V demands Luther to retract. The refusal of the reformer and the political protection of Frederick the Wise transform a theological dispute into a constitutional problem of the Empire.
Imperial forces defeat the French army and capture King Francis I.
Imperial mutiny troops plunder Rome during the Italian Wars.
The agreement legally accepts the coexistence of Catholic and Lutheran territories within the Empire and recognizes that religious unity can no longer be restored by mere imperial imposition.
Charles V progressively splits his domains between the Spanish branch and the Austrian branch of the Habsburgs.
Philip II's naval expedition against England fails after fighting, logistical problems and adverse temporary.

eventos.titulo: Charles V is elected King of the Romans
eventos.descripcion: The succession of Maximilian I turns the imperial election into a European competition. Charles gathers the imperial crown with a dynastic heritage extending from the Netherlands to Spain and America.
In the absence of a male heir, Charles VI attempts to ensure the indivisibility of Habsburg domains and the succession of his future daughter Mary Theresa.
Philip Melanchthon presents to Charles V a systematic exhibition of Lutheran faith, supported by several princes and cities of the Empire.
Charles V defeats the Esmalcalda League and captures its two great leaders, but the military victory fails to restore the religious unity of the Empire.
The death of Francis of Anjou makes Enrique de Navarra an alleged heir. Enrique de Guisa reorganizes the Catholic League, backed from Spain, to prevent a Protestant from inheriting the French crown.

Alfonso V of Aragon defeats the Angevin resistance and enters Naples. For the first time since Vespers, the same monarch controls Aragon, Trinacria and the continental kingdom, although the crowns retain separate identities.

eventos.titulo: Alfonso's inheritance is once again separated
eventos.descripcion: At the death of Alfonso V, Aragón and Trinacria pass to their brother John II, while Naples remains for his son Fernando. Personal union does not become a stable fusion of crowns.

eventos.titulo: France and Aragon are distributed Naples
eventos.descripcion: Louis XII and Ferdinand the Catholic agree to divide the kingdom of Frederick I. Cooperation lasts little: disputes over the boundaries of partition make the former allies enemies.

eventos.titulo: Cerignola: the Grand Captain changes the war
eventos.descripcion: The forces of Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba defeat the French in Cerignola. The combined use of infantry, campaign fortification and firearms consolidates the Aragonese position in southern Italy.
A second great victory of the Grand Captain forces the French forces to withdraw. The balance born of the 1500 cast is definitely broken in favour of Fernando.

eventos.titulo: Ferdinand gathers Naples and Trinacria under his crown
eventos.descripcion: The French defeat leaves Ferdinand the Catholic as king of Naples in addition to Trinacria. The two parts of the former Sicilian monarchy once again share sovereign, although they will continue to be administered as distinct kingdoms.

eventos.titulo: Pius V gets the Holy League
eventos.descripcion: Pius V achieves an agreement between the Hispanic Monarchy, Venice and the Pontifical States. Philip II provides an essential part of the resources and his half-brother Don Juan of Austria receives the supreme command of the allied fleet.

eventos.titulo: The king's resignation does not force the island
eventos.descripcion: Jaime II agreed to abandon his Sicilian claim in Anagni, but the Sicilians refused to return to the Angevin domain. They chose their brother Federico and forced the Casa de Barcelona to divide over the future of the island.

Mary and Martin came to Sicily with Aragonese support to impose themselves on the barons. The Queen’s hereditary legitimacy was not enough without military capacity. The island’s government was once again closely linked to the Crown of Aragon.

historias.titulo: Burgundy: The Kingdom That Was Not

people.resumen: King of Aragon who consolidated the Mediterranean projection of the Crown after the Sicilian crisis. His diplomacy and alliances placed the house of Aragon at the heart of Western Mediterranean politics.
The Commitment of Caspe chose him to succeed Martin I, inaugurating the Trastámara branch of Aragon. Previously he had exercised the regency of Castile during the minority of John II.
King of Aragon and conqueror of Naples, where he established a court that became one of the great humanist foci of the 15th century.

King of Aragon and Navarre, central figure of the dynastic conflicts of the Iberian peninsula of the 15th century. He was the father of Fernando the Catholic and key piece in the expansion of the Trastámara.

King of Aragon and, together with Isabel I, protagonist of the dynastic union of Hispanic crowns. His politics combined peninsular consolidation, Mediterranean expansion and intense marriage diplomacy.
Queen of Castile and Aragon, daughter of the Catholic Monarchs and mother of Charles V. He retained his crowns while Philip, Ferdinand and Charles successively exercised the government.

name: Kartli
summary: The Eastern kingdom retained a royal branch Bagrationi after the division of Georgia. Persia and the Ottomans intervened in their appointments, wars and depositions. The reigns of Simon, Rostom and the Vajtang show different strategies of resistance and collaboration. Since 1762 their joint succession with Kajetia was consulted in Kartli-Kajetia.
notes: The Kingdom of Eastern Georgia, with sovereignty conditioned by Persia and Ottoman interventions.

Simon I continues Luarsab's resistance.
